- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), often peaking too high and then falling too fast.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too low a mean, fails to anticipate rebound from lows.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility — forecasts show more noise than actual price path smoothness.
- Fails to capture seasonal or event-driven spikes (e.g., policy changes, weather, or market sentiment) in the first 7–10 days.
- Underestimates the magnitude of upward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Often underestimates the true mean of the 30-day window, especially when the true mean is above 72.0.
